lines.text: Today you will practise real-life English for restaurants, shops, phone calls and asking for help.
Start requests with could I or can I, and add please.
Could I have a glass of water, please?
It sounds much kinder than give me water.
Say could I have, or I would like, then the food and please.
I would like a masala dosa, please.
When the food comes, say thank you.
Ask do you have, and how much is it?
Do you have a blue notebook?
How much is it?
Start with hello, this is, and your first name.
Ask may I speak to, and the person’s name, please.
End with thank you, bye.
Start with excuse me to get attention politely.
Excuse me, could you help me, please?
Ask a grown-up you trust, like a teacher, a parent or a shop helper at the counter.
Listen to Riya order food at a restaurant.
The waiter says, Good evening! What would you like?
Riya says, Could I have a masala dosa, please?
Anything to drink? A mango lassi, please. Here you are. Thank you!
Riya used please twice and thank you once. That is polite and confident.
Now listen to Arjun at a stationery shop.
Excuse me, do you have a blue notebook? Yes, we do. Here it is.
How much is it? It is forty rupees.
I will take it, please. Thank you!
Last, listen to Zoya make a phone call to her friend.
Hello, this is Zoya. May I speak to Meera, please?
Sorry, she is not at home. Can I take a message?
Yes, please. Could you tell her I called? Thank you. Bye!
Great work! Let’s remember what we learned.
Now build along, then try the challenges. You’ve got this!
